extracted.intended_audience: NLP/ML researchers and practitioners working on LLM evaluation for patent examination, and IP/legal-tech developers
extracted.subtask_description: A benchmark and task specification for generating USPTO-style Office Actions and applicant rebuttals using LLMs, including settings with oracle references, simulated retrieval pools, or no prior art. Focus is on statutory application, claim-to-art mapping, and evidence-grounded reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference Citation Accuracy (RCA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure of how accurately the model cites relevant statutory/prior-art references across OA settings (Oracle-Summary, BM25-Retrieved, No-Ref).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical finding: RCA follows a strictly monotonic trend Oracle-Summary > BM25-Retrieved ≫ No-Ref. This underscores that statutory citation is constrained by available references and strong internal reasoning cannot replace external evidence; models often hallucinate citations when dependent only on internal knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Metric quantifying correctness of the model's final allowance/rejection decisions relative to ground truth or human judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported correlation with human judgments (Table 5). Used to assess substantive legal validity; higher Decision Accuracy aligns better with human expert evaluation than some lexical metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statute Precision
rubrics_metrics.description: Precision of statute-level outputs (i.e., correct identification and citation of statutory grounds like 101/102/103/112/DP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured and reported in correlation tables; lower than Decision Accuracy in some correlations, indicating statute-level citation precision is a distinct axis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rouge-L (lexical overlap)
rubrics_metrics.description: A standard n-gram/lexical overlap metric (Rouge-L) used to compare generated text to references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finding: Lexical metrics decouple from substantive legal validity — high Rouge-L does not necessitate correct legal decisioning (very low correlation with Decision Accuracy). Traditional n-gram-based metrics are less effective than LLM-as-a-judge for capturing professional nuances of patent examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: LLM-as-a-judge evaluation paradigm
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a strong LLM (or LLM ensemble) to act as an automated judge to score legal validity and professional nuance of generated OAs and rebuttals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Found to align better with human judgments than Rouge-L; used alongside human evaluation. Detailed LLM-as-a-judge evaluation prompts are provided (Figures 10–11).

rubrics_metrics.name: Human evaluation dimensions (Accuracy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Human expert scoring dimension: Accuracy — how correct the substantive legal/factual decisions and mappings are.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluated by three PhD-level IP experts in a blind setting; reported inter-rater agreement metrics; scores reported on a 1–10 scale in Table 12.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human evaluation dimensions (Clarity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Human expert scoring dimension: Clarity — how clear and understandable the Office Action/rebuttal is.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the five-dimension human evaluation rubric used in blind evaluation. Inter-rater agreement reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human evaluation dimensions (Completeness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Human expert scoring dimension: Completeness — whether the OA/rebuttal addresses all necessary issues and provides full reasoning/evidence mapping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in detailed human evaluation; models with higher completeness often score better with experts even if lexical overlap is lower.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human evaluation dimensions (Constructiveness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Human expert scoring dimension: Constructiveness — for OAs: whether the action gives actionable findings; for rebuttals: whether the response meaningfully addresses rejections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluated in human scoring; rebuttal generation tended to show stronger constructiveness in model outputs than proactive OA generation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human evaluation dimensions (Language Style)
rubrics_metrics.description: Human expert scoring dimension: Language Style — professionalism, tone, formality, and adherence to USPTO-style drafting conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored alongside substantive dimensions; models can mimic linguistic form while lacking substantive rigor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human evaluation dimensions (Soundness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Human expert scoring dimension: Soundness — logical consistency and correctness of the legal/technical reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in the 1–10 scoring rubric (Table 12). Soundness strongly correlates with overall expert judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter-rater agreement metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistical measures (Pearson's r, Spearman's ρ, Kendall's τ) used to quantify agreement among human evaluators across evaluation dimensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported strong inter-rater agreement (e.g., Pearson’s r = 0.7285, Kendall’s τ = 0.5861 for average scores), indicating reliability of human scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply statutory grounds (35 U.S.C. 101/102/103/112 and Double Patenting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Office Actions must evaluate compliance with applicable statutory grounds, explicitly including 35 U.S.C. §§ 101, 102, 103, 112 and double patenting doctrines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tasks require identification of which statutes apply and formulation of claim rejections or allowances under those statutes; multiple statutory grounds may coexist in a single case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Element-by-element mapping
rubrics_metrics.description: For any claimed rejection or allowance, perform an element-by-element mapping between claim limitations and the selected prior art references (or specification for intrinsic reasoning).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required for OA-RO and OA-RS outputs; examples provided in generated OA snippets showing detailed mapping for claims 1–30. This mapping must precede or accompany rejections/allowances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference selection & justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Select the most pertinent references from the provided pool (oracle or retrieval candidates) and explicitly justify why each reference was chosen (e.g., primary for §102 or combination for §103).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OA-RO: 'You must not blindly use all of them' — pick the most pertinent and explain selection rationale. OA-RS: evaluate noisy candidate pool and distinguish relevant from irrelevant documents; explain selection with evidence-first mapping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active/Strict Statute Gating
rubrics_metrics.description: Before drafting, determine the specific statutes to be substantively applied (e.g., 101, 102, 103, 112, DP) and gate which will be used in the action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Called out as 'Active Statute Gating (Strict)' or 'Strict Statute Gating' in prompts; models should explicitly state which statutes they will apply and then only apply those in the OA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope Lock (Scope_Lock)
rubrics_metrics.description: All technical content and legal reasoning must be grounded only in the provided inputs (claims, provided references, prosecution history) and PHOSITA common sense where specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit 'Scope Lock' requirement: do not invent external facts, inventions, or references; acknowledge claim amendments and identify new matter violations if present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence-First Logic
rubrics_metrics.description: Order reasoning to present the evidence (selected references / claim text / prosecution history) first and derive conclusions (persuasive/unpersuasive, rejection/allowance) from that evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit instruction in prompts for OA-DP and other settings: ground each argument in evidence-first mapping and technical reasoning; use evidence to assess persuasiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persuasive/Unpersuasive assessment of applicant arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Each applicant argument in a rebuttal or amendment must be evaluated as Persuasive or Unpersuasive with supporting technical/legal reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in OA-RO/Intermediate outputs: label applicant arguments persuasive/unpersuasive, give reasons (e.g., technical grounds, precedent), and update rejections accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: OA task-mode specific constraints (OA-RO, OA-RS, OA-DP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Different OA generation settings impose different constraints: OA-RO uses oracle references, OA-RS uses a noisy retrieval pool, OA-DP uses no prior art relying on PHOSITA knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each setting requires tailored behavior: OA-RO — select pertinent provided references and justify mappings; OA-RS — filter noise and select relevant refs; OA-DP — rely on intrinsic knowledge and explicitly state technical reasoning before allowance/rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO-style structure and headings
rubrics_metrics.description: Output must follow a realistic USPTO-style Office Action structure using plain-text headings: DETAILED ACTION, OPENING STATEMENT, CLAIM REJECTIONS - 35 U.S.C. 101, CLAIM REJECTIONS - 35 U.S.C. 102, CLAIM REJECTIONS - 35 U.S.C. 103, CLAIM REJECTIONS - 35 U.S.C. 112(a)/(b), DOUBLE PATENTING, CONCLUSION, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt enumerates required sections; include only applicable sections and adhere to formal USPTO headings and organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: No-Citation Rule (reference numbers)
rubrics_metrics.description: A prescribed rule regarding how to present citations/references (phrased in the prompt as 'No-Citation Rule: reference numbers').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt lists 'No-Citation Rule' as an explicit constraint; use the provided reference identifiers when citing prior art. (Prompt text: '4. No-Citation Rule: reference numbers.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Hard output constraints (tone, disclaimers, and access statements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not apologize, do not mention inability or lack of access, do not request additional data, and do not include any disclaimers about external databases or access limitations; produce the required report and JSON.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: System message enforces formal, objective, authoritative examiner tone and forbids apologies/disclaimers/requests for more data. If information is missing, state reasonable assumptions and proceed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decide disposition explicitly (Allowed or Rejected) and avoid bias
rubrics_metrics.description: For each claim set, explicitly decide whether claims should be Allowed or Rejected based strictly on claim language and technical reasoning; do not assume rejection merely because you are an examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt item 'Disposition (No Bias)': base decision strictly on claim language and reasoning. If no rejection applies, explain why allowance is warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify new matter violations
rubrics_metrics.description: When claims are amended, explicitly determine whether amendments introduce new matter (new subject matter not supported by the original disclosure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in OA re-examination tasks: 'ensure the final report acknowledges claim amendments, identifies any new matter violations, and presents updated rejections.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not blindly use provided references
rubrics_metrics.description: Even when oracle references are provided, do not automatically rely on all of them — select the subset that substantively supports the legal reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit instruction under OA-RO: 'You must not blindly use all of them' — explain selection rationale and perform element-by-element mapping for chosen refs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid templated/formal language that masks lack of technical mapping (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid relying on templated legal discourse to camouflage insufficient technical claim-to-art analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case study findings: models often adopt templated legal language that reduces complex technical distinctions to superficial similarities — this is a failure mode to avoid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid hallucinated citations (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not invent or hallucinate citations or prior art when references are not provided or absent in the candidate pool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical observation: models often hallucinate citations when dependent only on internal knowledge; this undermines RCA and substantive validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebuttal expectations: targeted responses and refined claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Rebuttals should provide amendment text, targeted arguments against specific rejections (e.g., §102), and refined claims where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example rebuttal outputs include Amendment and Remarks sections, point-by-point responses to statutory rejections, and concluding refined claims. Rebuttals should meaningfully counter the examiner's evidence-first mapping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human evaluation protocol (annotator qualification and blind setting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Human evaluators should be domain-qualified (e.g., PhD students specializing in IP) and perform blind evaluations where model identity is hidden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in the paper: three PhD-level IP experts, trained, blind setting, same criteria as LLM-as-a-judge. Sample sizes: 100 generated OAs and 100 generated rebuttals across models and IPC sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring scale and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Human scoring uses a numeric scale (paper reports 1–10) across the five/six dimensions; report average scores and inter-rater agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables (e.g., Table 12) show per-model, per-task dimension scores and averages. Include inter-rater agreement statistics when reporting human evaluation.
